intervals.note: Start: the earliest collaboration-signed paper read (July 2008, a prototype at a shallow Chicago site); the formation date is not published in the sources read. Open end: the latest collaboration paper read is the 2014 data release / maximum-likelihood analysis (v3 February 2015); no source states that the collaboration has ended.

name: CoGeNT Collaboration
notes: No roster or member count was found; the Atlas records no memberships for this collaboration.

summary.plain: The small team of physicists who built and ran the CoGeNT germanium dark matter detector in the Soudan mine in Minnesota. Its members came from a US national laboratory, two universities and a detector manufacturer.
summary.technical: CoGeNT Collaboration (Coherent Germanium Neutrino Technology): authors from Pacific Northwest (National) Laboratory, the University of Chicago (Kavli Institute for Cosmological Physics, Enrico Fermi Institute), CANBERRA Industries and the University of Washington (CENPA) on the 2013 Phys. Rev. D paper; Duke University/TUNL appear on the 2014 data-release paper. No formation date, roster or member count is published in the sources read.
